transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, thanks. I guess the main reason I’m here is I’ve been having a hard time staying on track with things. It’s not like I’m trying to be careless or anything, but I’ll sit down to work on something—like an application—and then the tiniest thing can pull me away. A car outside, my phone buzzing, or even just some random thought, and suddenly I’m off doing something else before I really notice.

I don’t know if that makes sense, but it’s been getting in the way.
When did you first notice these difficulties with staying focused? Were you able to stay on task better when you were younger, or has this been a long-standing issue?

I think it’s been there for a long time, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible kid or anything, but even in elementary school my teachers would move my seat around because I’d talk when I wasn’t supposed to.

And I remember forgetting homework kind of a lot, or rushing through worksheets and making dumb careless mistakes. So… yeah, I guess it wasn’t just something that started recently. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
As you were growing up, did you ever feel like you had trouble sitting still, or like you were always moving or fidgeting, even when you were trying to stay calm?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I was like bouncing off the walls all the time or anything, but I do think I’ve always been kind of… restless, I guess.

Even now, if I’m sitting with someone, my leg is usually bouncing, or I’ll be clicking a pen, or messing with my keys without really noticing I’m doing it. Someone might point it out and then I’m like, “Oh, sorry.” So yeah, I guess that counts?
Have you ever found yourself acting quickly without thinking things through, like blurting out answers before being called on, interrupting others, or making snap decisions that got you into trouble?

Yeah… I mean, maybe not “trouble” trouble, but I do catch myself cutting people off more than I’d like.

Like with my mom, or even with a counselor, they’ll be talking and an answer just kind of pops into my head, and I say it before they’re finished. I’m not trying to be rude, honestly. It’s more like if I don’t say it right then, I feel like I’ll lose it. Then afterward I realize I interrupted and I feel bad. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
